title.en: Make sure you have health insurance

summary.en: Health insurance is mandatory in Germany. You usually need proof of it for your residence permit, your job or your university enrolment.

why.en: Without proof of insurance other steps (enrolment, employment, residence permit) can be blocked.

steps.en: Check whether you need public or private insurance for your situation.
Choose a provider and apply; keep the membership confirmation (PDF).
Give the confirmation to your university or employer.

note.en: Needed from your first day; ideally arranged before arrival.

label.en: Make it in Germany: health insurance

summary.en: Start with a prepaid SIM: you only need your passport — no bank account, no registered address, no credit check.

why.en: Banks, landlords, doctors and offices will ask for a German number, and some banks need one to open an account.

steps.en: Pick a prepaid provider below. You can switch later and keep your number.
Buy a starter kit in a supermarket or shop, or order an eSIM in the provider's app.
Verify your identity: a short video call with your passport (VideoIdent) or in a shop. The law requires it for every SIM.
Top up with vouchers from the supermarket checkout, a card or PayPal.
Once you have a registered address and a German bank account, you can move to a cheaper monthly plan.

documents.en: A smartphone with a camera for the video check

intro.en: All three are prepaid: no bank account, no registered address and no minimum term.

tag.en: Prepaid · O2 network · sold in every Aldi

pros.en: Starter kit at any Aldi Nord or Süd checkout
Top up with vouchers in cash at the checkout
Cheap: about €9 for 25 GB per 4 weeks

cons.en: O2 coverage is weaker in rural areas and on trains
Registration app and support are mostly in German

tag.en: Monthly, cancel any time · Telekom network · app only

pros.en: Telekom network: strong coverage, also outside cities
eSIM in the app — can be active the day you land
Pay with PayPal, so no German bank account needed

cons.en: No shops and no phone hotline — app and chat only

tag.en: Prepaid · O2 network · made for calls abroad

pros.en: Pay by international card or top up in cash

cons.en: O2 coverage, as with Aldi Talk
Data per euro is lower than the discount brands

note.en: Prices as checked in November 2026. Networks: Telekom, Vodafone and O2 run their own; most cheap brands use one of them.

tips.en: Avoid 24-month contracts in your first months: they need a credit check (Schufa) and are hard to cancel.
Put your German number into the bank and Anmeldung forms — offices often call or text.

summary.en: Everyone who moves into a home in Germany registers the address at the citizens' office (Bürgeramt) within two weeks — EU citizens too.

why.en: It is a legal duty, and many next steps depend on it: tax ID, bank account, residence permit.

steps.en: Book an appointment at your Bürgeramt as early as possible (slots can be scarce).
Ask your landlord for the landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung).
Fill in the registration form and bring all documents.
Keep the registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) — you will need it often.

note.en: Within two weeks of moving in. Late registration can be fined.

title.en: Apply for your residence permit before your visa ends

summary.en: Your national (D) visa is only the entry ticket. Apply for the residence permit at the foreigners' office (Ausländerbehörde) before the visa end date.

why.en: If you apply in time, your stay stays legal while they decide, and you can keep working if you were allowed to before. Appointments can take weeks.

steps.en: Check the end date on your visa.
Request an appointment at your Ausländerbehörde as soon as you have registered your address.
If the appointment is after your visa ends, send the application in writing before the end date and keep proof.
You may get a Fiktionsbescheinigung — a paper that confirms your stay while they decide.

documents.en: Fee: up to €110 for a first permit

note.en: Legal limit: the day before your visa ends. We remind you six weeks earlier.

label.en: Make it in Germany: residence permit

summary.en: You need a German or EU account (IBAN) for salary, rent and the health insurer. Online banks open in minutes with a passport; branch banks usually want your registered address first.

why.en: Rent, salary, insurance and many contracts in Germany run on direct debit (SEPA Lastschrift).

steps.en: Not registered yet? Start with an online bank below — many open without an Anmeldung.
Verify your identity with your passport in a video call.
Give your IBAN to your employer, landlord and health insurer.
Want a branch bank later? Open it after your Anmeldung and keep or close the online one.

tag.en: Online bank · German IBAN · app in English

pros.en: Opens in about 10 minutes by video call with your passport
Often no Anmeldung needed — check for your nationality in the app

cons.en: Needs a phone number to sign up

tag.en: Online bank · accepts more passport types

pros.en: Accepts more passports than most online banks

cons.en: Monthly fee — no free plan for a full account
Dutch bank: some forms may ask for a German IBAN (they must accept any EU IBAN)

tag.en: Local branch bank · in every town

pros.en: Branches and ATMs everywhere, help in person

note.en: Checked in November 2026. Rules for opening without an Anmeldung differ by nationality — the bank's app tells you.

tips.en: If a bank refuses you: anyone who lives legally in the EU has the right to a basic account (Basiskonto, § 31 Zahlungskontengesetz).
Employers and landlords must accept any EU IBAN for transfers and direct debits — a German one is not required by law.

summary.en: Check if your university includes a semester ticket; otherwise compare monthly passes.

steps.en: Students: check your semester ticket first.
Others: compare a nationwide subscription with local monthly passes.

summary.en: Finish enrolment (Immatrikulation) and get your student ID and enrolment certificate.

why.en: You need the enrolment certificate for the residence permit, insurance and discounts.

steps.en: Follow your university's enrolment checklist and deadline.
Pay the semester contribution.
Download your enrolment certificate.

title.en: Hand in your onboarding documents to your employer

summary.en: Your employer needs your tax ID, social security number, health insurance and bank details to pay you correctly.

why.en: Missing data can mean a higher emergency tax rate until it is fixed.

steps.en: Ask HR for their checklist.
Send the tax ID as soon as it arrives by post.

title.en: Watch your mailbox for your tax ID

summary.en: After your first address registration, your personal tax ID (Steuer-ID) is usually sent to you by post.

why.en: Employers need it for payroll; you need it for tax returns.

steps.en: Make sure your name is on your mailbox.
If it has not arrived after a few weeks, request it from the Federal Central Tax Office.

note.en: It can take up to six weeks after registration.

summary.en: Each home pays one broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag), €18.36 a month, however many people live there.

why.en: Unregistered households get letters and back-payments later. If a flatmate already pays, you may not need to.

steps.en: Ask flatmates whether the household is already registered.
If not, register online and check possible exemptions.

title.en: Meet people who arrived the same month

summary.en: Join a small coffee meetup with newcomers in your city.

why.en: The first weeks are the loneliest; people one step ahead of you are the best source of tips.

steps.en: Open the People tab and join the list for your city.

title.en: Find a home you can register

summary.en: You need an address where you can register (Anmeldung). Temporary stays count only if the landlord gives you a landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung).

why.en: Without a registered address you can't get a tax ID, and banks and offices will ask for it.

steps.en: Ask for the landlord confirmation before you sign.
Avoid listings that ask for money before a viewing.
If you stay with friends, they can give the confirmation too.

title.en: Apply for your residence permit within 90 days

summary.en: Your passport lets you enter without a visa and apply for a long-term residence permit from inside Germany (§ 41 AufenthV). Apply within 90 days of entry.

why.en: While your application is pending, your stay is allowed — but you may not work until the permit is issued.

steps.en: Register your address first.
Apply at your local Ausländerbehörde — many offices take online applications.
Keep the confirmation of your application (Fiktionsbescheinigung).

note.en: Legal limit: 90 days after entry. Apply early: no work until the permit is issued.

title.en: Check what your tourist stay allows

summary.en: A tourist (Schengen) visa or visa-free short stay usually can't be turned into a residence permit inside Germany. Get advice before it runs out.

why.en: Applying on a tourist visa doesn't extend your stay. Overstaying can block future visas.

steps.en: Note the last day of your allowed stay.
Talk to free migration counselling (MBE) about your options.

summary.en: Employers need your social security number (Sozialversicherungsnummer) to pay you. It comes by post from the pension insurance once you have statutory health insurance.

why.en: Without it, your first payroll can be delayed.

steps.en: Ask your health insurer if it hasn't arrived after a few weeks.
Give it to your employer.

title.en: Before a full-time job: switch your permit first

summary.en: With the Opportunity Card you may work up to 20 hours a week and do trial work. For a qualified full-time job you need a new residence permit — approved before you start.

why.en: Starting the job before approval is not allowed.

steps.en: When you get an offer, contact your Ausländerbehörde straight away.
Ask your employer for the documents the office needs.

label.en: Make it in Germany: Opportunity Card

summary.en: A licence from outside the EU is valid in Germany for six months after you take up residence. After that you need a German one.

why.en: Driving on an expired permission counts as driving without a licence.

steps.en: Check whether your country is on the Annex 11 list (e.g. Israel, Japan, Canada): then the swap needs no tests.
Otherwise expect theory and practical tests — start early.
Apply at your local driving licence office (Fahrerlaubnisbehörde) while your licence is still valid.

note.en: Legal limit: six months after you take up residence.

title.en: Get free advice on your asylum or protection case

summary.en: This plan is built for study and work moves. Asylum procedures and protection status have their own rules and deadlines, so talk to a free counselling service first.

why.en: Deadlines in asylum procedures can be short, and mistakes are hard to fix later. Counselling is free and confidential.

steps.en: Aged 27 or over: find a Migration Counselling for Adult Immigrants (MBE) office near you.
Aged 12–27: go to a Youth Migration Service (Jugendmigrationsdienst, JMD).
Bring all letters you got from BAMF or the Ausländerbehörde.

documents.en: All letters from BAMF and the Ausländerbehörde

title.en: You may get tax back for your first year

valueHint.en: Depends on your income and expenses; people who started work mid-year often overpay.

conditions.en: You were employed in Germany during the year.

howTo.en: File a tax return for the year after it ends (online via ELSTER or a tax app).

title.en: Check if you can join an integration course

valueHint.en: A state-funded German and orientation course. Places for voluntary participants are limited in 2026.

conditions.en: Many newcomers with a residence permit for work, family reasons or a long-term stay have a legal right to a place.
Since February 2026, BAMF has stopped admitting people who join voluntarily without a legal right.
From 1 August 2026, some groups can be admitted again if places are free — EU citizens among them.
Students usually have no right to a place: look at your university's language centre instead.

howTo.en: Your Ausländerbehörde tells you if you have a right to a course (or must take one). Otherwise ask a migration counselling service whether you can be admitted.

title.en: Free advice on recognising your qualifications

valueHint.en: Recognition can unlock better-paid jobs and some permit types.

conditions.en: You have a foreign vocational or university qualification.

howTo.en: Use the official recognition finder and book a counselling session.

valueHint.en: Some programmes pay a monthly stipend.

howTo.en: Search the DAAD scholarship database and ask your university about programmes it participates in.

title.en: Student discounts you can use from day one

conditions.en: Valid student ID or enrolment certificate.

howTo.en: Always ask for the student price (Ermäßigung) and check your university's benefits page.

valueHint.en: Free and confidential advice on permits, work, housing and family.

conditions.en: Adults 27 and over: Migration Counselling for Adult Immigrants (MBE), around 1,400 offices across Germany.

howTo.en: Find an office near you and book an appointment; many offer advice in several languages.

conditions.en: EU citizens and permanent residents are generally eligible.
With a residence permit, usually only if it allows you to work. Students: only while working.
Parent and child need tax IDs.

howTo.en: Apply to the Familienkasse once you have your tax IDs.

summary.en: Graduates from outside the EU can get a residence permit of up to 18 months to look for work. It can't be extended — apply before your study permit ends.
If you graduated in Germany, you can apply for a settlement permit after two years in qualified employment.

title.en: Permanent residence with the Blue Card

summary.en: 27 months of Blue Card work with basic German (A1), or 21 months with B1.
A settlement permit usually needs about five years of residence, B1 German and pension contributions. Some groups qualify sooner.
After five years of lawful residence you get a permanent right of residence automatically. It can be lost after more than two years abroad.
Naturalisation needs at least five years of lawful residence. The three-year fast track was abolished in 2025. Dual citizenship stays allowed.
